ir.texte: The city of Curitiba, in Brazil, is famous for its public transport. In the 1970s, planners decided to build special lanes for buses instead of an expensive underground railway. The buses stop at tube-shaped stations, where passengers pay before they enter, which makes boarding very fast. Today, about 70 percent of the city's residents use the bus system, and the city has less traffic than many cities of the same size. Visitors from around the world come to study the system, and many cities have copied the idea.
